title: Sigma-algebra
summary: A sigma-algebra is a collection of events stable under complementation and countable combination.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared set theory context is fixed.

content.plain: A sigma-algebra is a collection of events stable under complementation and countable combination.
content.exact: A σ-algebra 𝓕 on Ω is a family of subsets with Ω∈𝓕, A∈𝓕⇒Ω\A∈𝓕, and A₁,A₂,…∈𝓕⇒⋃ₙAₙ∈𝓕.
content.example: The power set of a finite sample space is a sigma-algebra.
content.caveat: The sigma-algebra specifies which subsets are measurable; not every subset must be admitted in every model.
